key_insight: Language models can be made better at knowing when to answer and when to abstain. In this study, a learned answer selector outperformed the base model by improving threshold-averaged utility on factual QA.
problem_solved: The paper tackles the challenge of calibration: helping a language model decide whether it is confident enough to answer or should say "I don't know" to avoid harmful mistakes.
method: Evaluate two strategies on Qwen3-14B: training the model to abstain directly versus training a separate component to select answers.
Use a utility-based score that rewards correct answers, penalizes wrong answers, and permits abstention.
Compare performance across three training seeds and two held-out confidence thresholds to test robustness and calibration.
impact: This work gives AI practitioners a practical path to reduce overconfident errors in factual QA systems. It is especially useful for deploying LLMs in settings where reliability and uncertainty awareness matter more than always answering.

paper_title: Can Language Models Learn When to Abstain? Policy Learning and Calibrated Answer Selection
paper_authors: Juan Terven, Diana-Margarita Córdova-Esparza, Ruben Gomez, Carlos Miranda Rocha, Julio-Alejandro Romero-González
